Senses.PreferredTarget: follow the waves and ride the swells

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Records use this phrase for moving responsively with the occasion, but Feiyin Tongrong turns it into criticism when the historical monastic in Zhaozhou's cypress case drifts with discriminating thought. The image is “follow the waves and ride the swells,” one member of the Yunmen three-phrase frame.
EvidenceBody: In the Blue Cliff Record, Yuanwu Keqin says a phrase can follow the waves when used on the road, meeting a knowing companion and distinguishing what the occasion calls for. His recorded sayings contrast going with the waves, where varied establishments are responsive at every point, with cutting off all streams and barring ordinary and sage.

Hongzhi Zhengjue says Yunmen, steady in body and mind, knew how to follow the waves. Tianyin Yuanxiu's verse follows waves and wind in a small boat but turns back rather than remaining midstream. Ruibai Mingxue defines the phrase-function through a shout that answers an affair with the affair and principle with principle. Feiyin Tongrong, by contrast, criticizes a monastic whose discriminating mind follows the waves and misses what is directly present; Shiyu Mingfang similarly says Yunmen “only managed” to follow the waves in a disputed case.

Senses.Note: Seven exact witnesses in seven independent works support one wave-following image with positive and critical stances; the stance changes, not the lexical object.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Following waves can mark exact responsiveness to the present affair, while the same movement becomes drift when driven by discriminating thought or secondhand wording.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: Feiyin and Shiyu use the phrase critically, and Tianyin's verse turns back rather than remaining midstream; adaptive movement cannot be reduced to passive conformity.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: Positive and critical passages evaluate the same wave-following action-image under different ownership and conditions.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Aliases cover literal wave language, the Yunmen classification, and the common go-with-the-flow lookup while explanation controls the passive-drift overreading.

ModifierControls.Finding: 隨 and 逐 both mark movement with wave and swell; the witnesses determine whether that movement is responsive or merely drifting.

FamilyControls.Finding: Companion cutoff function that Yuanwu explicitly contrasts with wave-following.
Companion encompassing function within Yunmen's three-phrase frame.
